title: Word Order 1: Objects, Place and Time
summary: Keep a verb and its object together, and put descriptions of how an action happens in a natural position. When both place and time come at the end of a sentence, place usually comes before time.
learningObjectives: Keep a direct object next to its verb instead of inserting a time or manner expression between them.
Place a manner expression such as carefully or very well after a direct object.
Use the usual order place + time at the end of a sentence.
Rearrange everyday statements without changing their meaning or verb tense.

explanation.heading: Keep the verb and its object together
explanation.body: An object answers questions such as what? or whom? after a verb. In ordinary sentences, keep the verb and its direct object together. Do not put an expression about time or manner between them.
explanation.example: Rita folded the towels after breakfast.

explanation.heading: Put manner after the object
explanation.body: When a verb has a direct object, expressions that say how something is done normally follow that object: read the message carefully, speak French fluently, or enjoy the meal very much. Without an object, a manner adverb often follows the verb.
explanation.example: The guide explained the route clearly.

explanation.heading: Put place before time
explanation.body: When both expressions follow a verb, a neutral, common order is place first and time second. Place says where something happens; time says when, how long or how often. Other orders can be possible for emphasis, but practise this common pattern first.
explanation.example: We ate lunch in the garden on Sunday.

explanation.heading: Keep the object before a place expression
explanation.body: A sentence can include an object, a place and a time. A useful default order is subject + verb + object + place + time. Do not interrupt a short verb–object combination with a place expression.
explanation.example: I left my notebook at the office yesterday.

left.label: Natural order
left.note: The object the guitar comes before beautifully.

right.label: Word order to avoid
right.note: The manner word separates the verb from its short direct object.

left.label: Place + time
left.example: The family met at the café after work.
left.note: At the café gives the place; after work gives the time.

right.label: Time + place (not the default here)
right.example: The family met after work at the café.
right.note: This is possible in context, but place + time is the neutral order practised in this lesson.

examples.sentence: Theo reads his emails carefully in the morning.
examples.note: The object his emails comes before the manner adverb carefully.

examples.sentence: We visited our grandparents in the countryside last weekend.
examples.note: The place phrase precedes the time phrase.

examples.sentence: The children finished their puzzles quickly.
examples.note: The direct object comes immediately after finished.

examples.sentence: My neighbour works at a bakery every Saturday.
examples.note: The place comes before the frequency expression.

examples.sentence: I left my umbrella on the train this morning.
examples.note: The object, place and time appear in a useful neutral sequence.

commonMistakes.why: Do not put a manner adverb between a verb and its short direct object.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Tariq bought yesterday a new backpack.
commonMistakes.correct: Tariq bought a new backpack yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: Put the direct object after bought; the time expression usually follows it.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We left on the bus our coats.
commonMistakes.correct: We left our coats on the bus.
commonMistakes.why: Put the short object our coats before the place phrase.
The object Spanish comes before the manner phrase very well.

studyTips: After an action verb, ask “what?” or “whom?” to find the object; keep the object next to the verb.
For everyday descriptions, practise this sequence: verb + object + place + time.
Remember that place before time is a useful default, not an absolute rule for every context.

exercises.feedback: The object short stories follows reads, and quietly describes how Nina reads.

exercises.prompt: We washed ___ before the guests arrived.
exercises.feedback: The direct object the windows follows washed, and carefully says how we did the washing.

exercises.prompt: Choose the usual neutral order (object, place, time): I left ___ .
choices: at the office yesterday my scarf
my scarf yesterday at the office
my scarf at the office yesterday
exercises.feedback: The neutral sequence is object (my scarf), place (at the office), then time (yesterday).
Keep the object the rules together after explains; clearly follows it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the words in brackets in a natural order: He ___ . (every night / his homework / does)
exercises.feedback: Does comes before its object his homework; every night follows the verb–object pair.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the words in brackets in a natural order: The chef cut ___ . (carefully / the bread)
exercises.feedback: A manner adverb normally follows the direct object the bread.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the words in brackets using place before time: They arrived ___ . (at noon / at the museum)
exercises.feedback: At the museum tells us where, and at noon tells us when.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the words in brackets: I bought ___ . (this morning / some flowers)
exercises.feedback: Some flowers is the object of bought; the time phrase comes afterwards.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Ella washed carefully the dishes.
exercises.feedback: The direct object the dishes belongs immediately after washed.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I yesterday bought a new notebook.
acceptedAnswers: I bought a new notebook yesterday.
exercises.feedback: In a neutral sentence, put the time phrase after bought a new notebook.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The nurse checked quickly my temperature.
acceptedAnswers: The nurse checked my temperature quickly.
exercises.feedback: The object my temperature comes before the manner adverb quickly.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I left at home my gloves.
acceptedAnswers: I left my gloves at home.
exercises.feedback: The short direct object my gloves comes before the place phrase at home.

speakingExercises.prompt: Put these parts into one complete sentence: “on Friday / we / visited / our cousins”.
acceptedAnswers: We visited our cousins on Friday.
speakingExercises.feedback: The direct object our cousins follows visited; the time comes at the end.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one complete sentence with verb + object + manner from these parts: “Rosa / opened / carefully / the parcel”.
speakingExercises.feedback: The object the parcel follows opened; carefully follows the object.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete neutral sentence, placing where before when: “Leo / runs / every afternoon / in the park”.
acceptedAnswers: Leo runs in the park every afternoon.
speakingExercises.feedback: The place phrase in the park precedes the time expression every afternoon.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one past-tense sentence from these cues: Liam / carefully / the plates / carry. Start with Liam and put the manner word after the object.
speakingExercises.feedback: The direct object the plates comes immediately after carried; carefully follows the object.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change to the usual place-before-time order. Keep The children played at the beginning, without adding or removing words: The children played after lunch in the courtyard.
acceptedAnswers: The children played in the courtyard after lunch.
speakingExercises.feedback: The place in the courtyard normally comes before the time after lunch when both are at the end.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks where and when you found your jacket. Facts: under the sofa; on Monday. Begin 'I found my jacket' and put the place before the time.
acceptedAnswers: I found my jacket under the sofa on Monday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Keep the object my jacket after found, then give the place under the sofa and the time on Monday.

speakingExercises.prompt: Your friend says: Dad likes very much this song. Correct only the word order, keep Dad likes at the beginning, and say the whole sentence.
acceptedAnswers: Dad likes this song very much.
speakingExercises.feedback: The object this song must stay next to likes; very much comes after the object.

speakingExercises.prompt: Give one short update using these cues: yesterday / the brakes / the mechanic / at the garage / carefully / checked. Begin with The mechanic and use object, manner, place, then time.
acceptedAnswers: The mechanic checked the brakes carefully at the garage yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Checked the brakes stays together, followed by carefully, at the garage, and yesterday.

listeningExercises.audioText: We watched a film at my cousin’s house on Saturday.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where did they watch the film?
listeningExercises.feedback: The location mentioned is the cousin’s house.

listeningExercises.audioText: Ben left his wallet in the kitchen yesterday.
listeningExercises.prompt: When did Ben leave his wallet there?
listeningExercises.feedback: Yesterday is the time expression at the end of the sentence.

listeningExercises.audioText: My brother reads comic books on the bus every morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word direct object immediately after “reads”.
listeningExercises.feedback: Comic books is what the brother reads; it follows the verb directly.

listeningExercises.audioText: Maya hid the birthday present under her bed yesterday evening.
listeningExercises.feedback: The hidden object was a birthday present, so it was a gift.

listeningExercises.audioText: The bus driver left the spare tickets at the front desk this morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where should the staff look for the tickets?
listeningExercises.feedback: The front desk is the reception area; it is the place mentioned after the object.

listeningExercises.audioText: The pianist played the final song beautifully at the theatre last night.
choices: How well the song was played
listeningExercises.feedback: Beautifully describes the manner of playing, not the time or the size of the venue.

listeningExercises.audioText: The teacher explained the new game patiently after lunch.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the single word that tells how the teacher explained the game.
listeningExercises.feedback: Patiently describes the way the teacher explained the game and follows its direct object.

listeningExercises.audioText: We dropped the packages at the post office before breakfast.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word time expression at the end of the recording.
listeningExercises.feedback: Before breakfast is the final time expression, after the place at the post office.
